title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 02
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 02

questions.questionTextEn: During a reversible adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas,
questions.explanationEn: In an adiabatic process, $q = 0$, so $\Delta U = w$. During expansion, the gas does work on the surroundings ($w < 0$), hence $\Delta U = nC_{V,m}\Delta T < 0 \implies \Delta T < 0$ (the gas cools). Also, for a reversible adiabatic process, $\Delta S = 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of basicity in aqueous solution among piperidine, pyridine, and pyrrole is
questions.explanationEn: Piperidine has an $sp^3$-hybridized nitrogen lone pair ($\text{p}K_{aH} \approx 11.1$, strongest base); pyridine has a localized $sp^2$ lone pair ($\text{p}K_{aH} \approx 5.2$); pyrrole's lone pair is part of its aromatic $6\pi$ sextet, so protonation destroys aromaticity ($\text{p}K_{aH} \approx -3.8$, weakest base).

questions.questionTextEn: In the Baeyer–Villiger oxidation of unsymmetrical ketones with $m$-CPBA, the relative migratory aptitude of the following groups follows the order
optionsEn: methyl $>$ primary alkyl $>$ secondary alkyl $>$ tertiary alkyl
tertiary alkyl $>$ secondary alkyl $>$ primary alkyl $>$ methyl
primary alkyl $>$ secondary alkyl $>$ tertiary alkyl $>$ methyl
methyl $>$ phenyl $>$ tertiary alkyl $>$ secondary alkyl
questions.explanationEn: Migration in the Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement occurs toward an electron-deficient oxygen atom, so groups better able to stabilize partial positive charge migrate faster: $\text{H} > 3^\circ\text{ alkyl} > \text{cyclohexyl} > 2^\circ\text{ alkyl} \approx \text{Ph} > 1^\circ\text{ alkyl} > \text{Me}$. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: One mole of a pale-green hydrate isomer of $\text{CrCl}_3\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ reacts with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ to precipitate immediately $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$. The formula of this complex is
questions.explanationEn: Only ionizable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate immediately as $\text{AgCl}$. Precipitating $2\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ per mole of complex indicates two outer-sphere $\text{Cl}^-$ ions and one coordinated $\text{Cl}^-$, giving $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of diethyl ether ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$), the observed signals are
questions.explanationEn: Both ethyl groups are equivalent by symmetry: the six $\text{CH}_3$ protons couple to $2$ adjacent $\text{CH}_2$ protons ($n+1 = 3$, triplet, $6\text{H}$), and the four $\text{CH}_2$ protons couple to $3$ adjacent $\text{CH}_3$ protons ($n+1 = 4$, quartet, $4\text{H}$).

questions.questionTextEn: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2xy$ satisfying the initial condition $y(0) = 3$ is
questions.explanationEn: Separating variables gives $\frac{dy}{y} = -2x\,dx$. Integrating yields $\ln y = -x^2 + C \implies y = A e^{-x^2}$. Applying $y(0) = 3$ gives $A = 3$, so $y = 3e^{-x^2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to VSEPR theory, the molecular geometry of $\text{XeOF}_4$ is
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{XeOF}_4$, xenon ($8$ valence electrons) forms one $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bond ($2$ electrons) and four $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ single bonds ($4$ electrons), leaving $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5 + 1 = 6$ (octahedral electron geometry), with the lone pair trans to the $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ bond, giving a square pyramidal molecular geometry ($C_{4v}$).

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the operator commutator $\left[x, \dfrac{d}{dx}\right]$ is
questions.explanationEn: Acting on an arbitrary differentiable test function $f(x)$: $\left[x, \frac{d}{dx}\right]f(x) = x\frac{df}{dx} - \frac{d}{dx}(xf) = x\frac{df}{dx} - f - x\frac{df}{dx} = -f(x)$. Hence $\left[x, \frac{d}{dx}\right] = -1$.

questions.questionTextEn: A reaction $A \to P$ yields a straight line with a positive slope when $1/[A]_t$ is plotted against time $t$. The $y$-intercept and slope of this plot, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: For a second-order reaction $A \to P$ with $-d[A]/dt = k[A]^2$, integration yields $\frac{1}{[A]_t} = \frac{1}{[A]_0} + kt$. Plotting $1/[A]_t$ versus $t$ gives a straight line with $y$-intercept $1/[A]_0$ and slope $k$.

questions.questionTextEn: Among pyrrole, pyridine, and piperidine, the correct order of Brønsted basicity in aqueous solution is
questions.explanationEn:
- **Piperidine** ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx 11.1$): localized lone pair in an $sp^3$ orbital $\implies$ strongest base.
- **Pyridine** ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx 5.2$): localized lone pair in an $sp^2$ orbital (higher $s$-character holds electrons tighter) $\implies$ moderate base.
- **Pyrrole** ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx -3.8$): nitrogen lone pair is part of the $6\,\pi$ aromatic sextet; protonation destroys aromaticity $\implies$ extremely weak base.
Thus, **piperidine $>$ pyridine $>$ pyrrole**. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: When an aqueous mixture of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is titrated conductometrically with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, the conductance versus volume of $\text{NaOH}$ plot shows
optionsEn: three linear segments: an initial sharp decrease, a gentle increase up to the second equivalence point, and a final steep increase.
two linear segments: a sharp decrease followed directly by a steep increase.
three linear segments: an initial sharp increase, a flat plateau, and a final decrease.
three linear segments: an initial gentle increase, a sharp decrease, and a final steep increase.
questions.explanationEn: First, strong acid $\text{HCl}$ is neutralized (fast $\text{H}^+$ replaced by slow $\text{Na}^+ \implies$ sharp decrease). Next, weak acid $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is neutralized to strong electrolyte $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ ($\implies$ gentle increase). Finally, excess $\text{NaOH}$ adds fast $\text{OH}^-$ ions ($\implies$ steep increase).

questions.questionTextEn: According to the Irving–Williams series, the thermodynamic stability constants ($\log K$) of high-spin octahedral complexes of divalent first-row transition metal ions with a given nitrogen/oxygen donor ligand follow the order
questions.explanationEn: Across the $3d$ divalent series, decreasing ionic radius and increasing CFSE stabilize complexes from $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($d^5$, CFSE $= 0$) to $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($d^8$). $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($d^9$) gains extra stabilization from Jahn–Teller distortion (peaking at $\text{Cu}^{2+}$), while $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$, CFSE $= 0$) drops sharply: $\text{Mn}^{2+} < \text{Fe}^{2+} < \text{Co}^{2+} < \text{Ni}^{2+} < \text{Cu}^{2+} > \text{Zn}^{2+}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of 2-bromopyridine with sodium methoxide ($\text{NaOMe}$) in methanol proceeds much faster than that of 3-bromopyridine because
optionsEn: nucleophilic addition at C2 places negative charge directly on the electronegative ring nitrogen atom in the Meisenheimer-like intermediate
3-bromopyridine is sterically hindered by the ring nitrogen lone pair
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ of halopyridines, nucleophilic attack at **C2** (or C4) allows the negative charge of the anionic $\sigma$-complex to be delocalized directly onto the **electronegative ring nitrogen**, strongly stabilizing the transition state. Attack at **C3** cannot place negative charge on nitrogen, making 3-bromopyridine much less reactive. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Addition of dibromocarbene ($:\text{CBr}_2$, generated from $\text{CHBr}_3$ and $t\text{-BuOK}$) to $(Z)$-but-2-ene yields
questions.explanationEn: Dibromocarbene ($:\text{CBr}_2$) generated by $\alpha$-elimination of $\text{CHBr}_3$ with $t\text{-BuOK}$ is a **singlet carbene** (stabilized by lone-pair donation from $\text{Br}$ into the vacant $2p$ orbital). Singlet carbenes undergo concerted, stereospecific *syn* cyclopropanation of alkenes (Skell's rule), converting $(Z)$-but-2-ene exclusively into ***cis*-1,1-dibromo-2,3-dimethylcyclopropane**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the hydrolytic polymerization of methylchlorosilanes to prepare silicones, the monomer used as a **chain-terminating (end-capping) unit** and the monomer used as a **cross-linking unit**, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: Hydrolysis of $\text{Me}_3\text{SiCl}$ yields $\text{Me}_3\text{SiOH}$, which has only one $-\text{OH}$ group and therefore caps (terminates) polymer chains. Hydrolysis of $\text{Me}_2\text{SiCl}_2$ yields linear chains, while $\text{MeSiCl}_3$ produces $\text{MeSi(OH)}_3$ with three condensation sites, generating 3D cross-linked silicone resins.

questions.questionTextEn: A pure solid melts at $300\text{ K}$ under $1\text{ bar}$ pressure with $\Delta H_{\text{fus}} = 6.00\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and molar volume change $\Delta V_{\text{fus}} = V_l - V_s = +1.00 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Using the Clapeyron equation, increasing the pressure by $100\text{ bar}$ ($1.00 \times 10^7\text{ Pa}$) shifts the melting point by approximately
questions.explanationEn: By the Clapeyron equation, $\frac{dT}{dP} = \frac{T\Delta V_{\text{fus}}}{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}$. Hence $\Delta T \approx \frac{300 \times (1.00 \times 10^{-5}) \times (1.00 \times 10^7)}{6000} = +5.0\text{ K}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The rate of nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) of 1-halo-2,4-dinitrobenzenes with piperidine in methanol follows the order
optionsEn: all four react at identical rates
questions.explanationEn: In the addition–elimination $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ mechanism, **nucleophilic addition** to form the anionic Meisenheimer $\sigma$-complex is rate-determining (carbon–halogen bond cleavage occurs in the fast second step). Fluorine, being the most electronegative halogen, makes the *ipso* carbon most electrophilic and stabilizes the negative charge of the Meisenheimer intermediate most strongly, giving the order **$\text{Ar}-\text{F} \gg \text{Ar}-\text{Cl} \approx \text{Ar}-\text{Br} > \text{Ar}-\text{I}$**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The differential expression $(2xy + 3y^2)\,dx + (x^2 + kxy)\,dy$ is an exact differential if the constant $k$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: For $M\,dx + N\,dy$ to be exact, Euler's reciprocity relation requires $\frac{\partial M}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial N}{\partial x}$. Here $\frac{\partial M}{\partial y} = 2x + 6y$ and $\frac{\partial N}{\partial x} = 2x + ky$. Equating gives $k = 6$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following substituted biphenyls is **optically active** (resolvable into stable atropisomers at room temperature)?
questions.explanationEn:
Stable biphenyl atropisomerism requires (i) bulky *ortho* substituents to prevent rotation about the C1–C1' bond, AND (ii) unsymmetrical substitution on **each** ring ($a 
eq b$ and $c 
eq d$). 6,6'-Dinitrobiphenyl-2,2'-dicarboxylic acid has bulky $-	ext{NO}_2$ and $-	ext{CO}_2	ext{H}$ at the four *ortho* sites ($-	ext{NO}_2 
eq -	ext{CO}_2	ext{H}$ on both rings). 2,2',6,6'-Tetranitrobiphenyl is symmetric on both rings (achiral); 4,4'-dinitrobiphenyl-2,2'-dicarboxylic acid has only two *ortho* groups (rotates freely); 2,2'-difluorobiphenyl has tiny $	ext{F}$ atoms (rapid racemization).

questions.questionTextEn: $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{NaF}$ both crystallize in the rock-salt ($\text{NaCl}$) structure with nearly identical interionic distances ($r_0 \approx 210\text{ pm}$ and $231\text{ pm}$, respectively) and similar Born exponents ($n \approx 7$). According to the Born–Landé equation, the ratio of lattice energy magnitudes $|U_0(\text{MgO})| / |U_0(\text{NaF})|$ is closest to
questions.explanationEn: By the Born–Landé equation, $|U_0| = \frac{N_A A |z_+ z_-| e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)$. Since $A$ and $n$ are essentially identical for rock-salt $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{NaF}$, $\frac{|U_0(\text{MgO})|}{|U_0(\text{NaF})|} \approx \frac{|(+2)(-2)|}{ |(+1)(-1)|} \times \frac{231}{210} = 4 \times 1.1 = 4.4$.

questions.questionTextEn: At saturation just below the critical micelle concentration (CMC), a surfactant forms a close-packed monolayer at the air–water interface with surface excess $\Gamma_{\max} = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ mol m}^{-2}$. Taking $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, the cross-sectional area occupied by a single surfactant molecule is closest to
questions.explanationEn: The area per molecule is $a = \frac{1}{N_A \Gamma_{\max}} = \frac{1}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 4.0 \times 10^{-6}} = 4.151 \times 10^{-19}\text{ m}^2 = 41.5\text{ \AA}^2$ (since $1\text{ m}^2 = 10^{20}\text{ \AA}^2$).

questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-2-phenylethan-1-one ($4\text{-MeO-C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{Ph}$) with $m$-CPBA affords as the major ester product
questions.explanationEn: In the Baeyer–Villiger oxidation, the electron-rich **4-methoxyphenyl group** ($+\text{M}$ $-\text{OMe}$ substituent strongly stabilizes partial positive charge in the migration transition state) has a significantly higher migratory aptitude than the primary benzyl group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{Ph}$). Insertion of oxygen between the carbonyl carbon and the 4-methoxyphenyl ring yields **4-methoxyphenyl 2-phenylacetate**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
For the complete combustion of $1\text{ mol}$ of liquid benzene at $300\text{ K}$:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6(l) + \dfrac{15}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \longrightarrow 6\text{CO}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
the value of $\Delta H - \Delta U$ is closest to
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Here $\Delta n_g = 6 - 7.5 = -1.5\text{ mol}$. Thus $\Delta H - \Delta U = \Delta n_g RT = (-1.5)(8.314)(300) = -3741\text{ J mol}^{-1} \approx -3.74\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In tetrasulfur tetranitride ($\text{S}_4\text{N}_4$), the molecular structure is best described as
optionsEn: a planar eight-membered ring analogous to cyclooctatetraene
a cradle-shaped ($D_{2d}$) cage with four coplanar nitrogen atoms and two weak transannular $\text{S}-\text{S}$ interactions
a cubic cage with alternating $\text{S}$ and $\text{N}$ vertices
two fused four-membered $\text{S}_2\text{N}_2$ rings linked by an $\text{N}-\text{N}$ bond
questions.explanationEn: $\text{S}_4\text{N}_4$ adopts a cradle-shaped cage of $D_{2d}$ symmetry in which the four $\text{N}$ atoms lie in a square plane, two $\text{S}$ atoms lie above and two below the plane, and the pairs of $\text{S}$ atoms on the same side exhibit weak transannular $\text{S}\cdots\text{S}$ bonding ($\approx 258\text{ pm}$).

questions.questionTextEn: Optically pure $(R)$-2-bromobutane has a specific rotation of $-23.1^\circ$. A sample of 2-bromobutane exhibits a specific rotation of $+13.86^\circ$ under identical conditions. The composition of the sample is
questions.explanationEn: Since pure $(R)$ has $[\alpha] = -23.1^\circ$, pure $(S)$ has $[\alpha] = +23.1^\circ$. The observed $+13.86^\circ$ indicates excess $(S)$ with $\text{ee} = \frac{13.86}{23.1} \times 100\% = 60\%$. Thus $\%(S) = \frac{100 + 60}{2} = 80\%$ and $\%(R) = \frac{100 - 60}{2} = 20\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the definite integral $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x e^{2x}\,dx$ is
questions.explanationEn: Integrating by parts with $u = x$, $dv = e^{2x}\,dx$: $\int_0^1 x e^{2x}\,dx = \left[\frac{x e^{2x}}{2}\right]_0^1 - \int_0^1 \frac{e^{2x}}{2}\,dx = \frac{e^2}{2} - \left[\frac{e^{2x}}{4}\right]_0^1 = \frac{e^2}{2} - \frac{e^2 - 1}{4} = \frac{e^2 + 1}{4}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the consecutive first-order reaction $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B \xrightarrow{k_2} C$ with $[A]_0 = 1.0\text{ M}$ and $[B]_0 = [C]_0 = 0$, if $k_1 = 0.20\text{ min}^{-1}$ and $k_2 = 0.10\text{ min}^{-1}$, the time $t_{\max}$ at which $[B]$ reaches its maximum and the value of $[B]_{\max}$, respectively, are
questions.explanationEn: For $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B \xrightarrow{k_2} C$, $t_{\max} = \frac{\ln(k_1/k_2)}{k_1 - k_2} = \frac{\ln 2}{0.20 - 0.10} = 10\ln 2\text{ min}$. The maximum intermediate concentration is $[B]_{\max} = [A]_0 \left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right)^{\frac{k_2}{k_1 - k_2}} = 1.0 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{0.10}{0.10}} = 0.50\text{ M}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the spinel $\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4$ (chromite) and the spinel $\text{NiFe}_2\text{O}_4$ (trevorite), the cation distributions are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4$, $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($d^3$) has a much larger OSPE ($0.84\Delta_o$) than high-spin $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$, $0.13\Delta_o$), so $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ occupies the octahedral sites (normal spinel). In $\text{NiFe}_2\text{O}_4$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($d^8$, OSPE $= 0.84\Delta_o$) strongly prefers octahedral sites over high-spin $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($d^5$, OSPE $= 0$), yielding an inverse spinel.

questions.questionTextEn: Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{1. O}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2, -78\,^\circ\text{C}; \text{2. Me}_2\text{S}$) of 1-methylcyclopent-1-ene yields
questions.explanationEn: Cleaving the endocyclic $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ double bond of 1-methylcyclopent-1-ene under reductive workup ($\text{Me}_2\text{S}$) converts the trisubstituted carbon ($\text{C1}-\text{Me}$) into a methyl ketone ($-\text{COCH}_3$) and the disubstituted carbon ($\text{C2}-\text{H}$) into an aldehyde ($-\text{CHO}$), yielding **5-oxohexanal** ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO(CH}_2)_3\text{CHO}$). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following operators is **Hermitian** on the space of square-integrable functions vanishing at $\pm\infty$?
questions.explanationEn: Integrating by parts shows $\left(\frac{d}{dx}\right)^\dagger = -\frac{d}{dx}$, so $\frac{d}{dx}$ is anti-Hermitian, while $\left(i\frac{d}{dx}\right)^\dagger = (-i)\left(-\frac{d}{dx}\right) = i\frac{d}{dx}$ is Hermitian (proportional to $\hat{p}_x = -i\hbar\frac{d}{dx}$). Meanwhile $\frac{d^2}{dx^2}$ is Hermitian, making $i\frac{d^2}{dx^2}$ anti-Hermitian.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following substrates fail to undergo standard Friedel–Crafts alkylation with $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$?
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Nitrobenzene** and **(C) Benzaldehyde** are strongly deactivated by $-M$ groups and do not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation.
- **(B) Aniline** has a basic lone pair that coordinates irreversibly to Lewis-acidic $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form the strongly deactivating $-\text{NH}_2^+\text{AlCl}_3^-$ complex, shutting down the reaction.
- **(D) Anisole** is strongly activated and readily undergoes Friedel–Crafts alkylation.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding the **anomeric effect** in pyranoses is/are correct?
optionsEn: It refers to the thermodynamic preference of an electronegative substituent (such as $-\text{OR}$ or $-\text{Cl}$) at the anomeric carbon (C1) to occupy the **axial** rather than equatorial position.

It is stabilized by hyperconjugative $n_\text{O} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C1}-\text{X}}$ orbital overlap between the axial lone pair of the ring oxygen and the antibonding orbital of the axial $\text{C1}-\text{X}$ bond.
It is generally stronger in nonpolar aprotic solvents than in highly polar protic solvents like water.
It always forces the anomeric substituent to adopt the equatorial orientation.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Electronegative C1 substituents prefer the axial orientation beyond what steric A-values predict.
- **(B) Correct:** Anti-periplanar $n_\text{O} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C1}-\text{X}}$ donation stabilizes the axial anomer (along with reduced dipole–dipole repulsion).
- **(C) Correct:** Nonpolar solvents do not screen dipole–dipole repulsion in the equatorial anomer, enhancing the axial preference.
- **(D) Incorrect:** The opposite (axial preference) is true.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Comparing a Morse anharmonic oscillator with a quantum harmonic oscillator, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: In an anharmonic oscillator, overtone transitions ($\Delta v = \pm 2, \pm 3, \dots$) become weakly allowed.
In an anharmonic oscillator, the spacing between consecutive vibrational energy levels decreases as $v$ increases.
A harmonic oscillator accurately predicts molecular bond dissociation at finite energy.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Anharmonicity relaxes $\Delta v = \pm 1$ to allow weak overtones, converges vibrational levels with increasing $v$, and shifts the zero-point energy to $G(0) = \frac{1}{2}\tilde{\nu}_e - \frac{1}{4}\tilde{\nu}_e x_e$.
- **(D) False:** A harmonic potential $V = \frac{1}{2}kx^2 \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$ and cannot describe bond dissociation.

questions.questionTextEn: For an **endothermic** gas-phase reaction ($\Delta_r H^\circ > 0$) with $\Delta n_g > 0$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: Increasing temperature increases the equilibrium constant $K_p$.
A plot of $\ln K_p$ versus $1/T$ has a negative slope.
Decreasing total pressure at constant temperature increases the degree of dissociation.
Adding a positive catalyst increases the equilibrium constant $K_p$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B) True:** By the van 't Hoff equation $\frac{d\ln K_p}{d(1/T)} = -\frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{R} < 0$, so $K_p$ increases with $T$.
- **(C) True:** Since $\Delta n_g > 0$, lowering pressure shifts equilibrium toward more moles of gas.
- **(D) False:** A catalyst speeds up attainment of equilibrium without changing $K_p$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about metallocenes is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Ferrocene ($[\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$) is diamagnetic and undergoes Friedel–Crafts acylation much faster than benzene.
Cobaltocene ($[\text{Co}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$) is a $19$-electron paramagnetic complex and a strong one-electron reducing agent.
Nickelocene ($[\text{Ni}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]$) is a $20$-electron paramagnetic complex with $2$ unpaired electrons.
Ferrocene is oxidized by mild oxidants to the $17$-electron ferrocenium cation $[\text{Fe}(\eta^5\text{-C}_5\text{H}_5)_2]^+$.
questions.explanationEn: All four statements are classic, verified properties of $3d$ metallocenes: ferrocene ($18\text{ e}^-$, diamagnetic, super-aromatic toward $\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$, oxidizes to $17\text{ e}^+$ ferrocenium); cobaltocene ($19\text{ e}^-$, $1$ unpaired electron, readily oxidizes to $18\text{ e}^-$ $[\text{CoCp}_2]^+$); nickelocene ($20\text{ e}^-$, $e_{1g}^{*2}$, $2$ unpaired electrons).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following metal–refining process pair(s) is/are **CORRECTLY** matched?
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Zone refining exploits greater solubility of impurities in the molten phase to produce ultrapure $\text{Si}$ and $\text{Ge}$.
- (B) True: Low-melting metals like $\text{Sn}$ and $\text{Pb}$ are separated from higher-melting impurities by liquation.
- (C) True: Mond process purifies $\text{Ni}$ via volatile $\text{Ni(CO)}_4$.
- (D) False: $\text{Zn}$ is refined by distillation or electrolysis (and does not form $\text{ZnI}_4$); van Arkel is used for $\text{Ti}$ and $\text{Zr}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding bimolecular reaction rate theories?
optionsEn: The steric factor $P$ in collision theory accounts for the orientation requirement of colliding molecules and is typically $\le 1$.
In Eyring transition state theory, $k = \frac{k_B T}{h} \exp\left(\frac{\Delta S^\ddagger}{R}\right) \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta H^\ddagger}{RT}\right)$.
A negative entropy of activation ($\Delta S^\ddagger < 0$) corresponds to a smaller pre-exponential factor $A$ (steric factor $P < 1$).
The harpoon mechanism (e.g., $\text{K} + \text{Br}_2$) has a steric factor $P \ll 1$.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. In the harpoon mechanism, long-range electron transfer creates a Coulombic attraction giving a reactive cross-section much larger than the hard-sphere cross-section, so $P > 1$, making (D) false.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following definite integral(s) evaluate(s) to **zero**?
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Zero:** $\sin^3 x$ is an odd function integrated over $[-\pi, \pi]$.
- **(B) Zero:** $x^3 e^{-x^2}$ is an odd function integrated over $[-2, 2]$.
- **(C) Zero:** $\int_0^{2\pi} \cos x\,dx = [\sin x]_0^{2\pi} = 0$.
- **(D) Positive:** $x^2 e^{-x^2} \ge 0$ everywhere and strictly positive for $x \neq 0$, so its integral is strictly positive.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compound(s) is/are **non-aromatic** (neither aromatic nor antiaromatic) in their ground state?
questions.explanationEn: Cyclooctatetraene adopts a non-planar tub shape to escape antiaromaticity (non-aromatic); cyclohepta-1,3,5-triene has an $sp^3$ $\text{CH}_2$ group (non-aromatic); $[10]$-annulene is forced out of planarity by internal $\text{H–H}$ steric clash (non-aromatic). $\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$ is aromatic.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following functional groups are reduced by $\text{LiAlH}_4$ in dry $\text{THF}$ (followed by aqueous workup) but are NOT reduced by $\text{NaBH}_4$ in methanol at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanationEn: $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a powerful hydride donor that reduces carboxylic acids (to $1^\circ$ alcohols), tertiary amides (to $3^\circ$ amines), and nitriles (to $1^\circ$ amines), whereas mild $\text{NaBH}_4$ does not reduce any of these three groups at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$. Both reagents rapidly reduce aldehydes (D). Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the axial chair conformation of methylcyclohexane, the number of gauche butane-like interactions between the axial methyl group and the ring carbons is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: An axial methyl group at C1 is gauche ($60^\circ$) to both the C2–C3 and C6–C5 ring bonds, creating $2$ gauche butane interactions (corresponding to $2 \times 0.9 \approx 1.8\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$).

questions.questionTextEn: For a zero-order reaction $A \to P$ with rate constant $k = 0.015\text{ mol dm}^{-3}\text{ min}^{-1}$ and initial concentration $[A]_0 = 0.80\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$, the concentration of $A$ remaining after $20\text{ min}$ is _______ $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*

In a $400\text{ MHz}$ $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrometer, a proton signal appears $1440\text{ Hz}$ downfield from $\text{TMS}$. Its chemical shift $\delta$ is _______ $\text{ppm}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: $\delta = \frac{\Delta\nu\text{ (Hz)}}{\nu_0\text{ (MHz)}} = \frac{1440}{400} = 3.60\text{ ppm}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The root-mean-square speed ($v_{\text{rms}}$) of helium gas ($M = 4.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) at $300\text{ K}$ is _______ $\text{m s}^{-1}$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Converting molar mass to SI ($M = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$): $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\frac{3 \times 8.314 \times 300}{4.0 \times 10^{-3}}} = \sqrt{1.87065 \times 10^6} = 1367.7\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 1368\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The number of $p\pi\text{--}d\pi$ bonds in one molecule of tetrahedral xenon tetroxide ($\text{XeO}_4$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: $\text{XeO}_4$ has four $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bonds arranged tetrahedrally around $\text{Xe}$ ($sp^3$ hybridized for the four $\sigma$ bonds), so it contains $4$ $p\pi\text{--}d\pi$ bonds.

questions.questionTextEn: A $2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ M}$ solution of a compound with molar absorptivity $\varepsilon = 4500\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$ is placed in a cell of path length $0.50\text{ cm}$. The absorbance of the solution is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: By the Beer–Lambert law, $A = \varepsilon c l = 4500 \times (2.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times 0.50 = 0.45$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a one-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator, the ratio of the energy in the $v = 2$ state to its zero-point energy ($v = 0$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Since $E_v = \left(v + \frac{1}{2}\right)h\nu$, we have $\frac{E_2}{E_0} = \frac{2 + 1/2}{0 + 1/2} = \frac{5/2}{1/2} = 5$.

questions.questionTextEn: Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{1. O}_3; \text{2. Me}_2\text{S}$) of $1\text{ mol}$ of 1,4-dimethylcyclohexa-1,4-diene produces _______ moles of 3-oxobutanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CHO}$).
questions.explanationEn: 1,4-Dimethylcyclohexa-1,4-diene has two symmetrical trisubstituted double bonds at $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ and $\text{C4}=\text{C5}$. Cleaving both double bonds under reductive conditions breaks the $\text{C}_8$ ring into **$2$** identical moles of the $\text{C}_4$ keto-aldehyde, 3-oxobutanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CHO}$).

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of $\pi$-electrons in a molecule of phenanthrene ($\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{10}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Phenanthrene has $7$ conjugated double bonds in its tricyclic aromatic framework, corresponding to $7 \times 2 = \mathbf{14}$ $\pi$-electrons.

questions.questionTextEn: In the radioactive decay transformation $^{232}_{90}\text{Th} \longrightarrow {}^{208}_{82}\text{Pb}$, the total number of $\beta^-$-particles emitted is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
From mass number balance, $n_\alpha = (232 - 208)/4 = 6$.
From atomic number balance: $90 = 82 + 2(6) - n_\beta \implies n_\beta = 94 - 90 = 4$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The de Broglie wavelength of a thermal neutron of kinetic energy $K = \dfrac{3}{2}k_B T$ at $T = 300\text{ K}$ is _______ $\text{\AA}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $m_n = 1.675 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$, $k_B = 1.3806 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}$, $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$]
questions.explanationEn: With $K = \frac{3}{2}(1.3806\times 10^{-23})(300) = 6.2127 \times 10^{-21}\text{ J}$, the de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_n K}} = \frac{6.626\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2(1.675\times 10^{-27})(6.2127\times 10^{-21})}} = 1.454 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \approx 1.45\text{ \AA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers possible for 4-chloropent-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{–CH}=\text{CH–CH(Cl)–CH}_3$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 4-Chloropent-2-ene possesses one disubstituted double bond capable of $(E)/(Z)$ isomerism and one independent stereocenter at C4 capable of $(R)/(S)$ isomerism, yielding $2 \times 2 = 4$ stereoisomers.

questions.questionTextEn: In *nido*-pentaborane(9), $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$ (square pyramidal $\text{B}_5$ core with one terminal $\text{H}$ on each boron), the number of $3\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ bridging bonds is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In $\text{B}_5\text{H}_9$, each of the $5$ boron atoms carries $1$ terminal $\text{H}$ atom ($5$ terminal $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds). The remaining $9 - 5 = 4$ hydrogen atoms bridge the four basal edges of the square pyramid, forming $4$ $3\text{c}\text{--}2\text{e}$ $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ bonds (styx code $4120$).

questions.questionTextEn:
In a Hantzsch pyridine synthesis, $2\text{ equivalents}$ of methyl acetoacetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Me}$), $1\text{ equivalent}$ of formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$), and $1\text{ equivalent}$ of $\text{NH}_3$ condense to form a 1,4-dihydropyridine, which is subsequently oxidized with $\text{HNO}_3$ to dimethyl 2,6-dimethylpyridine-3,5-dicarboxylate. The molecular weight of this pyridine derivative is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{N} = 14$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: Dimethyl 2,6-dimethylpyridine-3,5-dicarboxylate has the molecular formula $\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{13}\text{NO}_4$ (pyridine ring $\text{C}_5\text{HN}$ + two $-\text{CH}_3$ + two $-\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$). Molecular weight $= 11(12) + 13(1) + 14 + 4(16) = 132 + 13 + 14 + 64 = \mathbf{223}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ of $[\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ is $243\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The absorption maximum wavelength ($\lambda_{\max}$) of its $^2T_{2g} \to {}^2E_g$ transition is _______ $\text{nm}$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*

[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$; $c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$; $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn:
The energy of one mole of photons at $\lambda_{\max}$ equals $\Delta_o = \frac{N_A h c}{\lambda_{\max}}$.
$\lambda_{\max} = \frac{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.00 \times 10^8}{243{,}000} = 4.926 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 493\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Intramolecular McMurry coupling ($\text{TiCl}_3/\text{Zn-Cu}$) of octane-2,7-dione yields a cyclic alkene as the major product. The number of signals expected in the proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum of this product is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Intramolecular McMurry coupling of octane-2,7-dione ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO(CH}_2)_4\text{COCH}_3$) forms **1,2-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene**. By symmetry (plane bisecting $\text{C1}=\text{C2}$ and $\text{C4}-\text{C5}$), there are **$4$** chemically non-equivalent sets of carbons: (1) $\text{C1/C2}$ ($=\text{C}-$), (2) the two $-\text{CH}_3$ carbons, (3) allylic $\text{C3/C6}$ ($\text{CH}_2$), and (4) $\text{C4/C5}$ ($\text{CH}_2$).

questions.questionTextEn: The largest eigenvalue of the symmetric matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Setting $\det(A - \lambda I) = 0$ with $u = 2 - \lambda$ gives $u(u^2 - 2) = 0 \implies u = 0, \pm\sqrt{2}$. Thus the eigenvalues are $\lambda = 2, 2 - \sqrt{2}, 2 + \sqrt{2}$. The largest eigenvalue is $2 + \sqrt{2} \approx 3.41$.

questions.questionTextEn: When $2.44\text{ g}$ of benzoic acid ($M = 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) is dissolved in $100\text{ g}$ of benzene ($K_f = 5.12\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$), the freezing point is lowered by $0.5632\text{ K}$. Assuming benzoic acid forms dimers in benzene, the percentage association of benzoic acid is _______ $\%$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The stoichiometric molality is $m = \frac{2.44/122}{0.100} = 0.20\text{ mol kg}^{-1}$. Thus $i = \frac{\Delta T_f}{K_f m} = \frac{0.5632}{5.12 \times 0.20} = 0.55$. For dimerization ($n = 2$), $i = 1 - \frac{\alpha}{2} \implies \alpha = 2(1 - 0.55) = 0.90$, or $90\%$.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the linear pentapeptide **Lys–Arg–Ala–Gly–Glu** in aqueous buffer at $\text{pH } 7.0$. Given the approximate $\text{p}K_a$ values: $N$-terminal $-\text{NH}_3^+ = 9.0$, $C$-terminal $-\text{CO}_2\text{H} = 3.0$, Lys side chain $= 10.5$, Arg side chain $= 12.5$, and Glu side chain $= 4.2$, the predominant net integer charge on this pentapeptide at $\text{pH } 7.0$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
At $\text{pH } 7.0$, groups with $\text{p}K_a > 7.0$ are protonated and groups with $\text{p}K_a < 7.0$ are deprotonated:
- $N$-terminal $-\text{NH}_3^+$ ($+1$)
- $C$-terminal $-\text{CO}_2^-$ ($-1$)
- Lys side chain ($+1$)
- Arg side chain ($+1$)
- Glu side chain ($-1$)
Net charge $= (+1) + (-1) + (+1) + (+1) + (-1) = \mathbf{+1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the acid-catalyzed first-order inversion of sucrose, the optical rotation is $+30.0^\circ$ at $t = 0$, $+10.0^\circ$ at $t = 20.0\text{ min}$, and $-10.0^\circ$ at $t = \infty$. The first-order rate constant $k$ is _______ $\text{min}^{-1}$. *(round off to four decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For a polarimetrically monitored first-order reaction, $k = \frac{1}{t}\ln\left(\frac{\alpha_0 - \alpha_\infty}{\alpha_t - \alpha_\infty}\right) = \frac{1}{20.0}\ln\left(\frac{30.0 - (-10.0)}{10.0 - (-10.0)}\right) = \frac{\ln 2}{20.0} = 0.03466\text{ min}^{-1} \approx 0.0347\text{ min}^{-1}$.
